samples_reviewed.question_text: The two parts are 80 and 90. What is the sum?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: 7 of 8 samples correctly ask to round each addend to its own leading place and add (e.g. seed 42: 120 to 100, 136 to 100, sum 200; seed 45: 35 to 40, 180 to 200, sum 240 -- both hand-verified correct), but seed 55's read_fill_in_blank sample 'The two parts are 80 and 90. What is the sum?' never says estimate, never shows the approx symbol, and asks for an exact sum -- it exercises plain addition, not the estimation competency, the exact regression pattern this session's fix targeted.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Rounding directions are varied across samples (35 rounds up to 40, 24 rounds down to 20, 20 and 60 stay unchanged), but the competency text caps addends at up to 4 digits and none of the 8 sampled seeds show an addend above 180 (three digits) -- the near-ceiling 4-digit case is entirely unevidenced in this packet.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Vocabulary (estimate, sum, parts, true or false, is Jose correct) and sentence lengths are short and literal, matching Grade 3 reading level, and the Jose error-check framing in seed 50 is an appropriate light metacognitive task for this grade band.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Five formatters appear across the 8 seeds (mcq, cloze, error_detect, read_fill_in_blank, true_false), giving good structural spread, but every sample is either a bare numeral-pair stem or a flat dialogue frame like Jose says -- none embeds the estimate inside a real-world scenario such as money or measured objects, so contextual variety is thinner than formatter variety.

competency_alignment.rationale: For 7 of 8 seeds difficulty tracks addend digit-count and rounding complexity in a way that plausibly builds estimation skill, but seed 55's part-sum framing (80 plus 90 equals 170, an exact addition with no rounding step at all) decouples that sample entirely from the competency the other seven are progressing.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency text states addends of up to 4 digits, yet the largest number appearing in any of the 8 rendered samples is 180 (three digits) and seed 43 uses a single-digit addend (3) that cannot even be meaningfully rounded, so the sampled range sits well short of the stated ceiling.
